definitionBlock.heading: What is Native Shell (nsh) and nshm?
definitionBlock.body: Native Shell (nsh) is a Rust-first cross-platform framework where apps built in TSX or Rust render through native platform backends across desktop, mobile, GPUI, terminal, and web. Installable extensions, called nshm modules, plug into apps via nsh add. Awesome NSH curates verified nsh 0.7.1 packages, core crates, templates, and docs with index.json.

securityNotice.heading: Supply-Chain & Build Permission Notice
securityNotice.body: Installing a Rust, hybrid, or platform nshm runs its build.rs build script, procedural macros, and runtime code with your application's full local and runtime permissions. Crates can also contribute OS permissions, Info.plist descriptions, macOS entitlements, and HarmonyOS module entries through [package.metadata.nsh]. Review upstream source repositories and nsh.lock diffs before shipping any dependency.

installSourcesTable.intro: The nsh 0.7.1 CLI supports three remote package sources alongside local --path checkouts. Each source resolves differently in nsh.lock and reflects how maintainers publish 0.7-compatible releases.
rows: Published releases targeting nsh-core 0.7.x directly on Cargo's registry (nsh-extra, nsh-omarchy, nsh-icon, supernsh-icons, nsh-graph, nsh-o11y, nsmetry).

faqs.heading: Frequently Asked Questions About Native Shell & nshm

items.question: How do built-in nsh/* modules, installable nshm packages, and official framework crates differ?
items.answer: Built-in runtime modules imported from "nsh" ship directly inside the Native Shell engine and require no installation. Installable nshm modules are third-party or optional first-party packages added to nsh.json and nsh.lock with nsh add. Official framework crates like nsh-core, nsh-base, and nsh-platform-macos live inside longbridge/nsh, lack #[native_module] or nsh.json exports, and cannot be added with nsh add—either nsh manages them automatically or Rust applications depend on them via cargo add.

items.question: Why does nsh 0.7.1 not provide a built-in nsh search command?
items.answer: In nsh 0.7.1, the CLI focuses on explicit package coordinates: crate names on crates.io, github:owner/repo shorthands, Git URLs with optional --rev/--tag/--branch flags, and local --path directories. There is no central package registry index built into the CLI, which is why Awesome NSH runs six-channel discovery and publishes both human pages and index.json.

items.question: Why do 6 of the 13 verified nshm packages install from GitHub or a Git URL instead of crates.io?
items.answer: Several maintainers keep fast-moving 0.7 packages off crates.io temporarily: nsh-webgpu and nsh-skia explicitly set publish = false in Cargo.toml, nsh-shadcn and nsh-query have not published releases to crates.io, nsh-platform-harmonyos 0.1.0 on crates.io predated the "platform" manifest field required by nsh add (fixed in GitHub 0.1.1), and nsh-widgets 0.4.1 on crates.io and tag v0.4.1 still pins nsh: ^0.6 while its master branch updates to ^0.7.1.

items.question: Do all nshm packages require a Rust toolchain during app builds?
items.answer: No—only packages backed by Rust crates (rust-nshm, hybrid-nshm, and platform-nshm) require Cargo and rustc when building native hosts, plus wasm32-unknown-unknown (and sometimes LLVM clang/llvm-ar) for web builds. Pure TSX packages such as nsh-query have no Cargo.toml and ship TypeScript source bundled directly by nsh.

items.question: What does Awesome NSH verification test—and what does it not test?
items.answer: Automated CI runs `nsh add ...` for every installable entry inside a clean scratch nsh.json app on nsh 0.7.1, confirming manifest resolution and nsh.lock generation. It does NOT compile native binaries across physical iOS, Android, macOS, Windows, Linux, or HarmonyOS hardware, nor does it run upstream runtime UI test suites.

en.title: Installable nshm Modules for Native Shell 0.7.1
en.metaDescription: Compare 13 verified nsh add packages across UI kits, icons, canvas graphs, analytics, and HarmonyOS, with crates.io versus GitHub source guidance.
en.h1: Verified Installable nshm Modules (nsh 0.7.1)
en.lead: All 13 reusable Native Shell (nsh) modules verified with clean scratch-app `nsh add` runs on `nsh 0.7.1`, grouped across six functional categories.
intro: An installable nshm is not merely any crate prefixed with `nsh-` or tagged with `keywords = ["nshm"]` on crates.io. According to `crates/nsh-cli/src/nshm/manifest.rs` in `longbridge/nsh`, `nsh add` accepts a package only when it matches one of four structural manifest layouts—Rust (`#[native_module("...")]`), pure TSX (`nsh.json` `"exports"`), Hybrid (both), or Platform (`"platform": "<target>"`)—and satisfies semver checks against `nsh 0.7.1`.

This hub consolidates the 13 cleanly compatible modules verified across crates.io (7 modules plus 40 grouped icon-pack companion crates), `github:owner/repo` checkouts (5 modules), and Git branch pins (1 module). Unverified 0.6-era crates that only slip through `nsh add` because of Cargo's `[dependencies.nsh-core]` table normalization parser quirk are intentionally excluded here and documented on the Discovery page.

technicalCallout.heading: Grouped Icon Companion Crates & Version-Pin Workarounds
technicalCallout.body: To keep the directory readable instead of flooding listings with 40 repetitive sub-crates, the 5 icon packs under `nsh-icon` and the 35 Iconify set crates under `supernsh-icons` are documented inside their parent module pages. Note also that `nsh-widgets` and `nsh-platform-harmonyos` currently require GitHub sources (`--rev master` and `github:huacnlee/nsh-platform-harmonyos` respectively) because their published crates.io versions either pin `nsh: ^0.6` or lack the `platform` key.

comparisonTable.intro: Compare package architecture, source channel, and primary use case before choosing between overlapping modules in the same category.

Port of shadcn/ui new-york-v4 primitives (including Chat components) styled via Tailwind classes.
Shared Widget Tree IR for iOS WidgetKit/Live Activities, Android RemoteViews, KDE Plasma, and GNOME.

Interactive network/node-link graphs with force/hierarchical/circular/grid layouts and Rust acceleration.
High-throughput telemetry (TimeSeriesChart M4 pyramid, LogView, TraceWaterfall, FlameGraph).
Standard WebGPU API (`navigator.gpu`, `GPUDevice`, WGSL compute/render) backed by `wgpu 29`.
Declarative/imperative `react-native-skia` 2D drawing and `RuntimeEffect` shaders on macOS & Linux.
Pure-TSX TanStack Query hooks with zero Rust compilation and NSH Storage persistence.
Cookieless batched event & `<NavStack>` screen telemetry targeting self-hosted Cloudflare Workers.
Community ArkUI platform backend enabling `nsh run/package --target harmonyos` for HarmonyOS/OpenHarmony.

items.title: UI Kits: nsh-omarchy vs nsh-shadcn
items.body: Pick `nsh-omarchy` when you want zero-config crates.io installs, Omarchy desktop theme synchronization, and Tokyo Night or Flexoki Light defaults. Pick `nsh-shadcn` if your team already relies on shadcn/ui new-york-v4 semantics, Chat UI primitives, or `.app_class(...)` overrides and does not mind tracking GitHub head.

items.title: Icons: nsh-icon vs supernsh-icons
items.body: Choose `nsh-icon` when one of the five major MIT/Apache sets covers your app with minimal dependencies. Choose `supernsh-icons` when you need brand logos, country flags, specialty Iconify packs from 260 sets, or compiled `.ttf` glyph fonts—remembering that `--target web` needs LLVM `clang` and `llvm-ar`.

items.title: Graphics & Telemetry: nsh-graph, nsh-o11y, nsh-webgpu, nsh-skia
items.body: Use `nsh-graph` for topology diagrams and `nsh-o11y` for metrics, logs, traces, and flame graphs on NSH's built-in `<Canvas>`. Reach for `nsh-webgpu` when porting WebGPU shaders across desktop/mobile/web, or `nsh-skia` when you specifically need `react-native-skia` 2D paths and shaders on macOS and Linux.

en.title: Native Shell Framework Crates (Not nshm) Reference

en.h1: Framework & Official Crates (Not nshm)
en.lead: Reference index of all 19 official crates maintained inside `longbridge/nsh` at version `0.7.1`—explaining their architectural roles across Apple, Android, Windows, Linux, Web, GPUI, and TUI targets and why none install via `nsh add`.
intro: Developers auditing `nsh-core` reverse dependencies on `crates.io` (`107` raw crates returned, `18` official framework crates) frequently mistake the `19` official `longbridge/nsh` crates for installable `nshm` modules. Every crate listed in this section is strictly **not** an `nshm`: running `nsh add nsh-core` or `nsh add nsh-base` fails immediately on `nsh 0.7.1` with `no #[native_module("...")] at the crate's root`.

In Native Shell `0.7.1`, the `nsh` CLI automatically manages and links these `19` Apache-2.0 crates when building host targets for TypeScript TSX or Rust applications. Rust-first applications and `nshm` library authors declare crates such as `nsh-core`, `nsh-base`, `nsh-i18n`, or `nsh-testing` directly in `Cargo.toml` via Cargo (`cargo add nsh-core`) rather than inside `nsh.json` dependencies.

technicalCallout.heading: Why `nsh add` Rejects All 19 Official Framework Crates
technicalCallout.body: Inside `crates/nsh-cli/src/nshm/manifest.rs`, `Manifest::read` accepts a package only when it provides a Rust `[lib]` exporting `#[native_module("<specifier>")]`, a `Cargo.toml`-free `nsh.json` with `"exports"`, or a `nsh.json` declaring `"platform"` alongside a `nsh-platform-<target>` binary. Core libraries such as `nsh-core` (`0.7.1`) and `nsh-base` (`0.7.1`) supply Rust traits, reactive signals, layout shadow trees, and unstyled UI behavior instead of JS/TSX module bridges, while the `8` official platform backends compile directly through the CLI host pipeline rather than external `"platform"` manifests like `nsh-platform-harmonyos`.

comparisonTable.intro: The `19` official `0.7.1` crates divide into `11` Core Runtime & Tooling crates (`macOS`, `Linux`, `Windows`, plus cross-target libraries) and `8` Official Platform Backends.

en.h1: Native Shell Starter Templates, Examples & Reference Apps
en.lead: Curated starting points for Native Shell (`nsh 0.7.1`): official multi-mode examples, a production-style boilerplate, a mixed `ext/` Rust+TSX reference app, and the community showcase registry.
intro: End-user Native Shell applications built in mixed Rust and TypeScript TSX mode look remarkably similar to Rust `nshm` crates on disk because their `src/lib.rs` also exports `#[native_module("...")]` symbols. However, inspection on `nsh 0.7.1` confirms that repositories such as `SuperNSH/starter`, `huacnlee/spotish`, and `ryujane/Ferrix` configure `publish = false` in `Cargo.toml` and declare `"root"` or `"id"` in `nsh.json` instead of `"exports"`—meaning they are complete applications to clone and adapt rather than libraries to add with `nsh add`.

Awesome NSH isolates these `4` starter, example, reference-app, and showcase repositories (`longbridge/nsh Examples`, `SuperNSH/starter`, `longbridge/nsh-showcases`, and `huacnlee/disktree`) into a dedicated hub so newcomers can bootstrap desktop, mobile, or Web projects without mistaking full app templates for installable `nshm` dependencies.

technicalCallout.heading: App Boilerplate vs Installable `nshm` Manifest Signatures
technicalCallout.body: An installable library declares `"exports"` (for `tsx-nshm` or `hybrid-nshm`) or `"platform"` (for `platform-nshm`) in `nsh.json` without claiming an application `"id"` or `"root"` component. By contrast, application templates carry `"entry"` or `"root"` keys (`"root": "App"` in `SuperNSH/starter`), bundle identifiers, and app-local `ext/` Rust crates compiled inside the project itself rather than locked via `nsh.lock`.

en.title: nsh-extra: Official Device Modules for Native Shell
en.metaDescription: Opt into camera, location, photos, push, and speech via Cargo features in Native Shell 0.7.1, paying only the permissions and binary size you enable.
en.h1: nsh-extra: Official Optional Device Modules for NSH
en.summary: Official Cargo-feature-gated device capability package maintained in longbridge/nsh, exporting Camera, Location, Photos/PhotosPicker, Push, and Speech to TSX and Rust apps.

corePurpose.heading: Modular Device APIs Without Bloating Every App
paragraphs: Rather than bundling camera, geolocation, photo library, push notification, and speech recognition bindings into every Native Shell binary, `longbridge/nsh` places them in `crates/nsh-extra` behind Cargo features with `default = []`. The crate root registers `#[native_module("nsh-extra")]` so TSX code imports PascalCase namespaces such as `Camera` or `Location` from `"nsh-extra"`, while Rust apps call `nsh_extra::camera::take_photo` directly.

Each feature automatically activates only the OS frameworks and app-store declarations it needs. Inside `Cargo.toml`, `[package.metadata.nsh.features.<name>]` specifies per-feature `Info.plist` usage descriptions (`NSCameraUsageDescription`, `NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription`, `NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription`, `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription`, `NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription`), macOS sandbox entitlements, `UIBackgroundModes`, and Android manifest queries or `RECORD_AUDIO` permissions that `nsh` merges into the final app bundle.

useCasesAndTradeoffs.heading: When to Use nsh-extra & Feature Trade-offs
paragraphs: Choose `nsh-extra` whenever an application needs first-party camera capture, foreground geolocation, iOS photo library access, remote push delegate hooks, or streaming speech-to-text with official `nsh 0.7.1` parity and built-in test fakes (such as `speech::FakeSpeech`).

Because all five features start disabled by default, passing `--features` at install or editing `nsh.json` `"dependencies.nsh-extra.features"` prevents unused Apple privacy strings or Android permissions from triggering unnecessary App Store or Play Store review disclosures.
scenarios: Capturing photos with `Camera.takePhoto({ maxDimension: 2048 })` on iOS and Android without maintaining custom native camera bridges.
Embedding the native iOS photo picker view (`PhotosPicker` registered via `#[native_components(ios)]`) alongside reactive TSX screens.
Streaming interim speech transcripts on macOS, iOS, Android, Windows WinRT dictation, and the Web Speech API through one TypeScript interface.

installationAndSource.heading: Installation on nsh 0.7.1 & Source Details
installationAndSource.sourceRationale: Maintained in `longbridge/nsh` and published alongside the `0.7.1` framework release on crates.io, `nsh-extra` resolves straight from crates.io without Git URLs. Adjust `--features` to match only the capabilities your app enables (for example `--features camera,speech`).
prerequisites: Requires `nsh 0.7.1` and a local Rust toolchain matching the workspace edition.
Push on Android expects an external push service SDK binding alongside the iOS `remote-notification` background mode hook.
Community platform targets like `nsh-platform-harmonyos` may expose matching optional Cargo features (such as HarmonyOS HMS `speech`) when an `nsh-extra` feature is enabled.

platformSupport.heading: Per-Feature Platform Matrix
platformSupport.overview: Unlike uniform cross-platform UI crates, `nsh-extra` deliberately scopes each Cargo feature to the platforms that implement its underlying OS bridge in `0.7.1`.

matrix.notes: Desktop and Web are not implemented; Android adds an `IMAGE_CAPTURE` intent query rather than runtime camera permission.
Uses Apple CoreLocation on macOS/iOS and browser `navigator.geolocation` on Web; adds macOS `personal-information.location` entitlement.
Provides recent library reads (`Photos`) and layout-embedded `PhotosPicker` via `#[native_components(ios)]`.
Installs `UIBackgroundModes = ["remote-notification"]` on iOS; Android delegates manifest entries to your chosen push SDK.
Broadest feature: Apple Speech, Android `RecognitionService` + `RECORD_AUDIO`, Windows `Media_SpeechRecognition`, and Web Speech API.

companionsOrFeatures.heading: Available Cargo Features & Exported Modules
companionsOrFeatures.summary: Five independent features map 1:1 from Rust modules under `nsh_extra::*` to TSX namespaces in `"nsh-extra"`.

items.name: camera (Camera)
items.detail: System camera capture on iOS and Android (`tokio` optional dependency).

items.name: location (Location)
items.detail: One-shot or watched foreground location (`CoreLocation` on Apple, `web-sys` Geolocation on Web).

items.name: photos (Photos, PhotosPicker)
items.detail: Recent photo reads and embedded native `PhotosPicker` UI component on iOS.

items.name: push (Push)
items.detail: App delegate registration (`push::install`) and remote notification delivery hooks.

items.name: speech (Speech)
items.detail: Live speech recognition with interim transcripts across Apple, Android, WinRT, and Web.

verificationRecord.heading: nsh 0.7.1 Verification Record
verificationRecord.summary: Running `nsh add nsh-extra --features camera` in a clean scratch app on `nsh 0.7.1 (f78eace)` resolves `nsh-extra@0.7.1` from `crates.io` (`Apache-2.0`, updated `2026-11-25`) and records the enabled feature flag in `nsh.json` and `nsh.lock`.
verificationRecord.scopeDisclaimer: Scope boundary: automated CI checks `nsh add nsh-extra --features camera` manifest resolution and lockfile creation only. Actual camera hardware, CoreLocation prompts, WinRT dictation, and iOS `PhotosPicker` behavior require native device builds on target operating systems.

buildAndSecurityNote.heading: Build & System Permission Implications
buildAndSecurityNote.body: Because `nsh-extra` automatically merges `NSCameraUsageDescription`, `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription`, macOS sandbox entitlements, and Android permissions from `[package.metadata.nsh.features.*]` into your app manifest, enabling unused features can cause mobile app-store reviewers to ask why your binary requests restricted hardware access.

corePurpose.heading: 按 Cargo Feature 精细控制体积与系统权限
paragraphs: `nsh-extra` 位于官方仓库 `crates/nsh-extra`，根文件通过 `#[native_module("nsh-extra")]` 导出能力，并将 `default` 特性设为空列表。TSX 端直接从 `"nsh-extra"` 导入对应的大驼峰命名空间（如 `Camera`、`Location`、`PhotosPicker`），Rust 端则可直接调用 `nsh_extra::camera::take_photo` 等模块函数。

每个特性除了引入对应的系统框架依赖外，还在 `Cargo.toml` 的 `[package.metadata.nsh.features.<name>]` 中声明了打包所需的 `Info.plist` 权限提示文案（如 `NSCameraUsageDescription`）、macOS 沙盒 entitlements、后台推送标识及 Android 清单权限，由 `nsh` 构建时自动合并进应用配置。

useCasesAndTradeoffs.heading: 适用场景与按需裁剪取舍
paragraphs: 当应用需要调用官方维护、遵循 `nsh 0.7.1` 平台抽象并内置无头测试替身（如 `speech::FakeSpeech`）的原生硬件或系统能力时，`nsh-extra` 是首选方案。
相比把所有设备绑定塞进基础运行时，按 `--features` 按需启用能避免未使用的麦克风、相机或定位权限声明触发应用商店审核质疑，同时减小最终二进制体积。
scenarios: 在 iOS 与 Android 端通过 `Camera.takePhoto({ maxDimension: 2048 })` 调用系统相机拍照。
借助 `#[native_components(ios)]` 注册的 `PhotosPicker` 组件在 iOS 应用布局内直接嵌入原生相册选择器。
通过统一的 `Speech` 接口在 macOS、iOS、Android、Windows WinRT 与 Web 浏览器中实时获取语音识别中间文本。

en.title: nsh-omarchy: Theme-Following UI Kit for Native Shell
en.metaDescription: Built on nsh-base for Rust and TSX apps, this Omarchy-styled library tracks system colors live and falls back to Tokyo Night dark or Flexoki Light.
en.h1: nsh-omarchy: Live System-Themed UI Components for NSH
en.summary: A port of gpui-omarchy built atop nsh-base 0.7.0, offering nine UI families—from inputs and overlays to data tables and charts—for both Rust and TSX Native Shell apps.

corePurpose.heading: System Palette Tracking & Dual Rust/TSX Components
paragraphs: Authored by `huacnlee`, `nsh-omarchy` brings the Omarchy desktop aesthetic—square corners, a single accent color, foreground-tinted interaction states, clear focus rings, and compact keyboard-first controls—to Native Shell. `nsh-base` handles accessibility, focus routing, popups, and keyboard behavior, while `nsh-omarchy` renders the visual presentation.

At startup (`om::init()` in Rust or `Omarchy.followSystem()` in TSX), the library reads `~/.local/state/omarchy/current/theme/colors.toml` and subscribes to changes live. When running outside an Omarchy desktop environment—such as macOS, Windows, mobile, or Web—it falls back cleanly to built-in Tokyo Night (dark) or Flexoki Light palettes, or lets apps lock a palette via `Theme::tokyo_night().apply()` and `applyTheme(...)`.

useCasesAndTradeoffs.heading: Component Scope & Comparing with nsh-shadcn
paragraphs: Nine families cover Actions (`Button`, `Toggle`), Choices (`Checkbox`, `Switch`, `Slider`), Fields (`Input`, `NumberInput`, `OtpInput`, `Calendar`, `DatePicker`, `ColorPicker`), Navigation (`Tabs`, `Sidebar`, `Accordion`, `Menu`, `TitleBar`), Overlays (`Dialog`, `Sheet`, `Toaster`), Data (`DataTable`, `Tree`, `ResizablePanelGroup`), Display (`Markdown`, `Code`, `Keycap`), Charts (`LineChart`, `AreaChart`, `BarChart`, `PieChart` via `nsh-base/plot`), and Theme utilities.

Compared with `nsh-shadcn`, `nsh-omarchy` is already published on crates.io (`0.2.0`), embeds `nsh-base/plot` charts under default features, and natively mirrors Omarchy theme files. However, if your interface strictly requires shadcn/ui `new-york-v4` styling or prebuilt Chat message primitives, `nsh-shadcn` is closer to that design language.
scenarios: Desktop settings panels, developer utilities, and keyboard-centric tools built with `Sidebar`, `DataTable`, `Tree`, and `Keycap`.
Cross-platform apps sharing identical Rust and TSX theme tokens (`nsh_omarchy::tokens` or `themes/omarchy.json`) across light and dark modes.

en.metaDescription: Porting shadcn/ui new-york-v4 components (except form) to native desktop, mobile, and web views in Rust and TSX; install directly via GitHub.
en.h1: nsh-shadcn: Native Rust shadcn/ui new-york-v4 for NSH
en.summary: A Rust-backed component library by caoxing9 bringing shadcn/ui new-york-v4 components, Tailwind token classes, and AI chat primitives to both Rust and TSX NSH apps.

corePurpose.heading: Faithful new-york-v4 Primitives Rendered as Native Views
paragraphs: Rather than running React DOM or a WebView, `nsh-shadcn` implements shadcn/ui's `new-york-v4` registry directly in Rust atop `nsh-core = "0.7.1"` and `nsh-base = "0.7.1"` (with `plot` enabled for `Chart`). Each component preserves shadcn's Tailwind class strings alongside upstream source notes in `src/ui/*.rs` and exposes both Rust builder syntax (`ui::button("Save").outline()`) and TSX elements (`<Button variant="outline" size="sm" />`).

The component inventory spans seven groups: Actions (`Button`, `Button Group`, `Toggle`, `Toggle Group`), Basics (`Alert`, `Card`, `Kbd`, `Skeleton`, `Table`), Forms (`Checkbox`, `Field`, `Input`, `Input OTP`, `Radio Group`, `Switch`), Overlays (`Dialog`, `Drawer`, `Sheet`, `Sonner`, `Tooltip`), Menus (`Command`, `Combobox`, `Dropdown Menu`, `Select`), Layout (`Accordion`, `Calendar`, `Carousel`, `Chart`, `Resizable`, `Tabs`), and Chat (`Attachment`, `Bubble`, `Marker`, `Message`, `Message Scroller`, `Direction`). Upstream checks every component in light and dark mode against shadcn rendering and documents any intentional omissions (`form` is omitted in favor of `Field`).

useCasesAndTradeoffs.heading: Restyling, Partial Component Caveats & Choosing vs nsh-omarchy
paragraphs: Teams coming from React and shadcn/ui gain familiar variants, `.app_class(...)` tail-override customization on Rust elements, and built-in Chat UI elements (`Bubble`, `Message Scroller`, `Attachment`) without writing custom list virtualization or toast queues.

Note two explicit upstream caveats documented in the README: `Navigation Menu` opens on press rather than hover and omits shared viewports/indicators, and `Sidebar` omits mobile sheets, collapsed-state tooltips, sub-menus, badges/actions, and icon rails. Additionally, `Calendar` re-exports `chrono::NaiveDate` directly.
scenarios: AI assistant or chat applications utilizing `Bubble`, `Message`, `Message Scroller`, `Attachment`, and `Command` across desktop and mobile.
Web-originating teams wanting `new-york-v4` proportions and Tailwind class overrides inside native macOS, iOS, Android, Windows, or Linux hosts.
Mixed Rust/TSX codebases that appreciate an interactive browser gallery (`caoxing9.github.io/nsh-shadcn/`) compiled via NSH's Web target.

installationAndSource.heading: Why You Must Install nsh-shadcn via GitHub Right Now
installationAndSource.sourceRationale: Although the upstream README mentions `nsh add nsh-shadcn`, the crate returns HTTP 404 on crates.io as of `2026-11-26` (it has not been published to the Cargo registry yet). Install directly from GitHub using `nsh add github:caoxing9/nsh-shadcn`.
prerequisites: Requires `nsh >= 0.7.1` (`Cargo.toml` explicitly pins `nsh-core = "0.7.1"` and `nsh-base = "0.7.1"`).
Building the web gallery or targeting `--target web` requires LLVM with `wasm32` support on `PATH` (such as `brew install llvm` on macOS).

platformSupport.heading: Cross-Platform Rendering & Known Partial Controls
platformSupport.overview: Built on `nsh-core` and `nsh-base`, `nsh-shadcn` targets macOS, iOS, Android, Windows, Linux, and Web, with minor desktop/mobile navigation nuances.

matrix.notes: Renders native platform views; `Navigation Menu` triggers on press instead of mouse hover.
Upstream notes `Sidebar` currently lacks mobile sheet behavior and rail mode.
Compiled via `nsh package --target web` into `caoxing9.github.io/nsh-shadcn/` using LLVM wasm32.

companionsOrFeatures.heading: Crate Structure & Bundled Utilities
companionsOrFeatures.summary: Ships as a self-contained root library crate with bundled icons and date types; `gallery` and screenshots are excluded from packaged builds.

items.name: Built-in icon & date re-exports
items.detail: Exposes `nsh_shadcn::icon::{IconName, icon, labeled_icon}` and `chrono::NaiveDate` so apps do not need a separate `chrono` dependency.

items.name: `.app_class(...)` customization

items.name: DESIGN.md parity notes

en.h1: nsh-widgets: Cross-Platform Home Widgets & Live Activities
en.summary: Hybrid Rust + TSX nshm by SuperNSH that defines home-screen widgets, iOS Live Activities, Control Center controls, and Quick Settings tiles once in Widget Tree IR v1.

corePurpose.heading: One Declarative Widget Tree IR Across Four Native Widget Hosts
paragraphs: Native OS widgets cannot execute an application's main JS runtime inside home-screen extensions. `nsh-widgets` solves this with Widget Tree IR v1: apps describe widget UI once in TSX (`nsh-widgets/base`, `nsh-widgets/kit`) or Rust JSON (`nsh_widgets::update_data`), and shared native renderers draw the tree inside each OS extension model.

On iOS and macOS, `crates/nsh-widgets-cli` compiles a single Swift renderer (`NshWidgets.swift`) into WidgetKit extensions, covering home-screen families, lock-screen widgets, Live Activities (Dynamic Island), edit sheets, and iOS 18 Control Center controls. On Android, the crate bundles `android/nsh-widgets.aar` via `[package.metadata.nsh.android]` to drive RemoteViews, scrolling lists (API 31+), configure screens, and Quick Settings tiles. On Linux, the companion CLI generates KDE Plasma 5/6 QML plasmoids, GNOME Shell 45–51 extensions, Cinnamon 6 desklets, X11/Wayland `gtk-layer-shell` windows, and Waybar JSON output.

useCasesAndTradeoffs.heading: Interactive Actions, Companion CLI & Current Gaps
paragraphs: Widget buttons update shared store data even when the main app process is closed—via App Intents on Apple platforms and non-exported broadcast receivers on Android—and apps drain queued user actions through `take_actions`, `next_change`, or `Widgets.onChange(...)`.

According to upstream `README.md` (`0.4.1`, verified 23–24 Nov 2026 on emulators/VMs), Windows widget hosts, COSMIC applets, Wayland compositors without layer-shell, and physical iPhone/Android devices are NOT covered in `0.4.1` (use `nsh-widgets show --format waybar` for terminal or status-bar fallback).
scenarios: Shipping iOS Live Activities (compact/expanded Dynamic Island and lock screen) alongside Android Quick Settings tiles from one TypeScript tree.
Generating KDE Plasma plasmoids and GNOME Shell top-bar/popup widgets from the same store without writing separate QML or GJS extensions by hand.
Previewing multi-size widget layouts locally on desktop with `nsh-widgets preview --simulator` before building mobile extensions.

installationAndSource.heading: Why You Must Pass `--rev master` on nsh 0.7.1
installationAndSource.sourceRationale: Even though `nsh-widgets 0.4.1` exists on crates.io and as git tag `v0.4.1`, both still carry `"nsh": "^0.6"` in their published `nsh.json`, causing `nsh add nsh-widgets` and `nsh add github:SuperNSH/widgets` to fail on `nsh 0.7.1` (`nsh.json requires nsh ^0.6; this is nsh 0.7.1`). Passing the full HTTPS Git URL with `--rev master` pulls the updated `"nsh": "^0.7.1"` manifest.
prerequisites: Requires `nsh 0.7.1+` (uses `ios.extensions`, `macos.extensions`, `android.libraries`, and AAR manifest merging) and the companion `nsh-widgets` CLI (`cargo install nsh-widgets-cli` or GitHub releases).
Apple extensions require macOS with Xcode 26+ (`appintentsmetadataprocessor`); Live Activities need iOS 16.2+ and Control Center controls need iOS 18+.

Android builds require API 26+ (API 31+ for switches, rounded corners, and scrolling lists); Linux desktops require `kpackagetool5`/`6` or GNOME/Cinnamon/GTK 3 with `nsh-widgets` installed on the target machine.

zh.summary: SuperNSH 推出的混合型 nshm 模块，用统一的 Widget Tree IR v1 描述小组件界面，原生渲染至 iOS/macOS WidgetKit、Android RemoteViews、KDE Plasma 与 GNOME Shell。

corePurpose.heading: 统一 Widget Tree IR 桥接四大系统小组件宿主
paragraphs: 系统的桌面或锁屏小组件运行在独立扩展进程中，无法直接启动完整的 JS 宿主引擎。`nsh-widgets` 定义了 Widget Tree IR v1：应用在 TSX（`nsh-widgets/base`、`nsh-widgets/kit`）或 Rust JSON 中声明树形结构并喂入数据，再由各端通用原生渲染器完成绘制。

苹果端由配套工具 `nsh-widgets-cli` 将单一 Swift 渲染器（`NshWidgets.swift`）编译进 WidgetKit 扩展，同时支持锁屏小组件、Live Activities 灵动岛与 iOS 18 控制中心控件；Android 端通过 `[package.metadata.nsh.android]` 注入 `android/nsh-widgets.aar` 驱动 RemoteViews、API 31+ 滚动列表与快捷设置磁贴；Linux 端则可生成 KDE Plasma 5/6 QML 插件、GNOME Shell 45–51 扩展、Cinnamon 桌面插件、layer-shell 窗口及 Waybar JSON。

useCasesAndTradeoffs.heading: 无宿主交互机制与版本实测边界
paragraphs: 用户点击小组件按钮时，无需唤醒主界面即可通过 App Intent（Apple）或非导出广播接收器（Android）修改共享存储数据，主应用可通过 `take_actions`、`next_change` 或 `Widgets.onChange(...)` 消费变更。
据上游 `README.md` 说明，`0.4.1` 暂不提供 Windows 原生小组件宿主与 COSMIC applet，且未在实体 iPhone/Android 真机验证；纯终端或 Waybar 状态栏环境可使用 `nsh-widgets show --format waybar` 作为轻量输出。
scenarios: 希望用同一套数据模型同时覆盖 iOS 灵动岛实时活动、Android 桌面滚动列表与快捷磁贴。
为 Linux 桌面应用自动生成 KDE Plasma Plasmoid 与 GNOME 顶栏弹窗，免去手写 QML 与 GJS 扩展代码。
利用 `nsh-widgets preview --simulator` 在无真机时预览各尺寸小组件的明暗主题布局。

en.title: nsh-icon: Tree-Shaken SVG Icons for Native Shell
en.metaDescription: Pair the <Icon> and icon() renderer with five modular crates—Lucide, Heroicons, Tabler, Phosphor, or Remix—so only referenced vectors ship in builds.
en.h1: nsh-icon: Modular Tree-Shaken Vector Icons for NSH
en.summary: Apache-2.0 SVG icon renderer (`<Icon>`, `icon()`, `labeled_icon()`, `icon_set!`) paired with five standalone icon-pack crates covering over 21,900 curated vector icons.

corePurpose.heading: Zero-Bloat Vector Rendering Paired with Separate Pack Crates
paragraphs: Authored by `huacnlee`, `nsh-icon` replaces fragile Unicode symbols or emoji with theme-aware SVG vectors rendered in `currentColor`. By design, the `nsh-icon` crate itself holds zero icons; it provides the `Icon` type, Rust helpers (`icon()`, `labeled_icon()`, `icon_set!`), and the TSX `<Icon>` component (`size`, `strokeWidth`, `label`), while relying on `nsh-core` with the `svg` feature enabled.

Actual glyphs live in five dedicated sibling crates—`nsh-icon-lucide`, `nsh-icon-heroicons`, `nsh-icon-tabler`, `nsh-icon-phosphor`, and `nsh-icon-remix`—each named in PascalCase matching upstream conventions. Only the icon constants your code references are linked into the final binary and TSX bundle, keeping build sizes lean while automatically skipping decorative icons (`label` omitted) from screen readers.

useCasesAndTradeoffs.heading: Choosing Between nsh-icon and supernsh-icons
paragraphs: `nsh-icon` shines when a project uses one or two standard monotone UI icon sets and wants Apache-2.0 simplicity, minimal compile overhead, and per-icon tree shaking (`import { Search } from "nsh-icon-lucide"`). It also lets apps swap stroke widths cleanly on Lucide, Heroicons outline, and Tabler outline icons via `src_with_stroke_width(...)` or `strokeWidth`.

If your design requires full-color brand logos, country flags, animated spinners, `.ttf` glyph fonts, or any of ~255 niche Iconify collections beyond these five libraries, look at `supernsh-icons` instead.
scenarios: Standardizing UI navigation, toolbars, and button icons across Rust (`Lucide::Search`) and TSX (`<Icon icon={Search} />`) without icon fonts.
Ensuring accessible icon-only action buttons via `labeled_icon(Lucide::X, "Close")` or `<Icon label="Settings" />`.
Binding reactive signals directly to icons (`icon(move || if dark.get() { Lucide::Moon } else { Lucide::Sun })`).

installationAndSource.heading: Two-Step crates.io Installation (Renderer + Companion Pack)
installationAndSource.sourceRationale: Both `nsh-icon@0.2.2` and all five `nsh-icon-*` companion crates depend on `nsh-core = "0.7.0"` and publish directly to crates.io. Install `nsh-icon` first, then run `nsh add` for each icon pack you actually import.
prerequisites: Install at least one companion crate alongside `nsh-icon`, for example `nsh add nsh-icon-lucide`.

Requires `nsh-core` with `"svg"` feature active (automatically requested by `nsh-icon`, though `Cargo.toml` warns that disabling default features on `nsh-platform-*` without `svg` prevents rendering).
Requires Rust toolchain (and `wasm32` target when packaging for `--target web`).

platformSupport.heading: Cross-Platform SVG Vector Support
platformSupport.overview: Renders natively across all six core Native Shell targets wherever `nsh-core` `svg` support is active.

matrix.notes: Vector SVGs scale crisply across DPI factors and inherit surrounding `text_color` / `text-*` tokens.
Avoids platform font glyph inconsistencies and integrates with mobile screen-reader labels.
Tree-shaken SVG documents render cleanly inside NSH's WebAssembly DOM backend.

zh.metaDescription: 提供 <Icon> 与 icon() 渲染接口，并可按需搭配 Lucide、Heroicons、Tabler、Phosphor 或 Remix 五套独立图标包 crate 使用。
zh.h1: nsh-icon：可按需裁剪的模块化矢量图标渲染器
zh.summary: 由 huacnlee 维护的 Apache-2.0 图标渲染库，将核心 `<Icon>`/`icon()` 渲染器与 5 套主流图标包拆分为独立 crate，只把实际引用的矢量图标打入应用包。

corePurpose.heading: 渲染器与图标数据分离，按图标粒度 Tree-Shaking
paragraphs: 用普通字符或 Emoji 当作界面图标会受系统字体差异影响，也无法随主题改变线条粗细或被屏幕阅读器正确处理。`nsh-icon` 通过原生 SVG 矢量解决这一问题：它自身不包含任何图标，仅负责提供 `Icon` 类型、Rust 端 `icon()` / `labeled_icon()` / `icon_set!` 以及 TSX 端 `<Icon>`（支持 `size`、`strokeWidth` 与 `label`）渲染接口。
图标数据拆分为 `nsh-icon-lucide`、`nsh-icon-heroicons`、`nsh-icon-tabler`、`nsh-icon-phosphor` 与 `nsh-icon-remix` 五个独立子 crate。应用只下载用到的图标集，且在编译和打包阶段仅保留被导入使用的矢量图标；未设置 `label` 的装饰性图标会自动对屏幕阅读器隐藏。

useCasesAndTradeoffs.heading: 与 supernsh-icons 的定位差异与场景取舍
paragraphs: 如果应用主要使用上述五大主流单色线性/填充图标库，希望构建轻量、许可证统一为 Apache-2.0，且需要通过 `strokeWidth` 或 `src_with_stroke_width(...)` 精细调整描边粗细，`nsh-icon` 非常契合。
若项目中必须用到多色品牌 Logo、国旗、260 套 Iconify 里的冷门图标集或希望生成 `.ttf` 图标字体，建议选择同分类的 `supernsh-icons`。
scenarios: 在 Rust（`Lucide::Search`）和 TSX（`<Icon icon={Search} />`）中共用同一套跟随 `text-*` 主题色变化的矢量图标。
使用 `labeled_icon(Lucide::X, "Close")` 或 `<Icon label="Settings" />` 为纯图标按钮补充无障碍朗读标签。
直接把响应式信号传给图标函数（`icon(move || if dark.get() { Lucide::Moon } else { Lucide::Sun })`），随状态切换图标。

en.h1: supernsh-icons: 260 Iconify Sets, SVG & Font Glyphs for NSH
en.summary: Hybrid Rust + TSX icon system covering roughly 465,000 Iconify icons across 260 sets—with 35 crates.io companion crates, multicolor brand/flag support, and a .ttf icon-font builder.

corePurpose.heading: Full Iconify Breadth with Crate Packs, CLI Extraction & Fonts
paragraphs: `supernsh-icons` combines a single Rust-backed `<Icon>` renderer (`ui::icon()` for full SVG masks/filters, or NSH `Svg` via `icon(...)`) with TSX exports (`supernsh-icons/markup`, `supernsh-icons/iconify`) and the full Iconify catalog (~465,000 icons across 260 sets). Monotone icons automatically follow surrounding `currentColor` text styles, whereas logos, country flags, and emoji preserve their multi-color SVG fills.

The 35 most popular collections—including `lucide`, `ph`, `tabler`, `heroicons`, `ri`, `mdi`, `material-symbols`, `simple-icons`, `logos`, `circle-flags`, `fa7-*`, `fluent`, `carbon`, and `codicon`—publish as individual `supernsh-icons-<set>` crates on crates.io (`0.2.0`). For the remaining ~225 sets, or when you want a compact `.ttf` icon font (`<Glyph>` / `Root::font(FONT)`), the repository's `cli/nsh-icons.ts` tool writes only the icons or glyphs you specify.

useCasesAndTradeoffs.heading: Strengths, License Attribution & Web LLVM Requirement
paragraphs: Choose `supernsh-icons` over `nsh-icon` when you need brand logos (`logos`, `simple-icons`, `devicon`), circle/country flags (`circle-flags`, `flag`), UI icons from Material/Fluent/Carbon, SVG mask/filter fidelity (`ui::icon()`), or `.ttf` icon fonts for dense filled glyphs.

Keep two upstream constraints in mind: first, while the `supernsh-icons` library code is MIT, individual Iconify sets retain their upstream licenses (Font Awesome, Solar, Streamline, and Codicons carry CC BY 4.0 attribution terms, tracked in `NOTICE.md` and `docs/sets.md`); second, web builds require LLVM `clang` and `llvm-ar` alongside the Rust toolchain.
scenarios: Displaying multi-color tech logos (`logosRust`) and country flags alongside theme-tinted monotone icons in one `<Icon>` API.
Generating an app-specific `.ttf` glyph bundle (`supernsh-icons font ph:house-fill ph:heart-fill`) for filled Material or Phosphor glyphs.
Browsing and exporting styled PNG/JPEG/SVG app assets in the offline gallery hosted at `supernsh.github.io/icons/`.

Requires Rust toolchain (`nsh` compiles the crate even in TSX apps) and LLVM `clang` + `llvm-ar` for `--target web` builds.
Icon font mode (`supernsh-icons font`) rejects stroked outline icons (Lucide, Tabler) and multi-color icons; use SVG mode for those.

en.title: nsh-graph: Interactive Canvas Network Graphs in NSH
en.metaDescription: Force, hierarchical, circular, and grid layouts on native <Canvas> with community collapsing, OffscreenCanvas PNG export, and an optional Rust backend.
en.h1: nsh-graph: Interactive Network Graph Views for Native Shell
en.summary: Hybrid TSX + optional Rust network-graph module by JetSquirrel running on NSH's native <Canvas> across desktop, mobile, GPUI, and Web, drawing from gpui-graph and Neo4j NVL.

corePurpose.heading: Four Animated Layouts & Opt-In Rust Force Simulation
paragraphs: Authored by `JetSquirrel`, `nsh-graph` renders interactive node-link graphs onto NSH's native `<Canvas>` via `<GraphView>`, `<GraphLegend>`, `createGraphController()`, and `mergeGraphData()`. It implements four layouts—Barnes-Hut force-directed (d3-force style with collision, gravity, and group clustering), four-direction cycle-safe hierarchical, circular, and grid—along with animated transitions when switching layouts.

By default, the TypeScript engine handles smaller interactive graphs smoothly inside QuickJS. When node counts scale into the thousands, apps opt into `nsh-graph/native` (`setNativeBackend(native)`), moving `ForceLayout` simulation state and `GraphPainter` batched `Path2D` edge/node tracing into Rust (`native/src/lib.rs`) so QuickJS avoids per-frame array marshalling.

useCasesAndTradeoffs.heading: Rich Interaction Model, Accessibility & Local Checkout Tip
paragraphs: Built-in UX covers pan, wheel/pinch zoom, Shift-box multi-selection, neighbor hover tooltips, right-click context menus, arrow-key graph walking (`+`/`-`/`0`/`p`/`Esc`), community hull collapsing into `×N` super-nodes with bundled edges, an 8-category color-blind-validated palette, id-diffed `data` updates that preserve pinned positions, and PNG export via `controller.toImage()` on `OffscreenCanvas`.

Note an important optimization detail from upstream: crates.io and Git releases build the Rust backend optimized, whereas a local `--path` checkout inherits the app's debug profile unless `.cargo/config.toml` sets `[profile.dev.package.nsh-graph] opt-level = 3`. Upstream also notes `nsh-graph` relies on `onKeyDown`, `onPinch`, and `captureKeys` introduced in NSH 0.6+.
scenarios: Knowledge graphs, entity relationship explorers, and Neo4j-style dependency inspectors with neighbor expansion (`mergeGraphData`).
Clustered service or community topologies using collapsible group super-nodes (`×N`) and edge bundling.
Desktop/GPUI graph viewers scaling to 1,500–5,000+ nodes via opt-in `nsh-graph/native` Rust force layout and `GraphPainter`.

installationAndSource.heading: crates.io Installation & Opt-In Native Backend Wiring
installationAndSource.sourceRationale: `nsh-graph@0.3.0` (`nsh.json` `"nsh": ">=0.7"`, `Cargo.toml` `nsh-core = "0.7.0"`) is published directly on crates.io and also tagged on GitHub (`JetSquirrel/nsh-graph`). Install directly with `nsh add nsh-graph`.
prerequisites: Requires `nsh >= 0.7` and a local Rust toolchain (plus `wasm32-unknown-unknown` for Web builds).
The pure TSX view runs out of the box from `"nsh-graph"`; call `setNativeBackend(native)` once at startup with `import * as native from "nsh-graph/native"` to activate Rust acceleration.
For local `--path` development, add `[profile.dev.package.nsh-graph] opt-level = 3` in `.cargo/config.toml`.

platformSupport.heading: Cross-Platform `<Canvas>` Coverage Including GPUI
platformSupport.overview: Draws on NSH's built-in `<Canvas>` primitive rather than platform-specific GPU shaders, enabling identical support across seven targets.

matrix.notes: Upstream tests include headless engine/layout suites plus real host input checks (`nsh test example/input.test.tsx`).
Supports single-tap selection, double-tap activation, touch pan, and two-finger pinch zoom.
Explicitly listed alongside desktop/mobile/Web targets through NSH `<Canvas>`.
Interactive gallery published at `jetsquirrel.github.io/nsh-graph/` via `wasm32-unknown-unknown`.

en.title: nsh-o11y: Observability Charts for Native Shell
en.metaDescription: Render TimeSeriesChart, LogView, TraceWaterfall, and FlameGraph panels with M4 min/max pyramid decimation, createChartSync, and an optional Rust store.
en.h1: nsh-o11y: High-Throughput Observability Charts for NSH
en.summary: Hybrid TSX + optional Rust telemetry visualization suite by JetSquirrel delivering TimeSeriesChart, LogView, TraceWaterfall, FlameGraph, SandwichView, ServiceMap, and Heatmap.

corePurpose.heading: M4 Pyramid Decimation & Two-Layer Native Canvas Architecture
paragraphs: Built specifically for observability dashboards rather than generic business charts, `nsh-o11y` stores columnar time-series samples inside a min/max pyramid (blocks of 8, 64, 512, ...) and renders each pixel column via M4 decimation (first, min, max, and last values). As a result, rendering work scales with screen width rather than raw sample count while never hiding single-sample spikes or dropouts.

Charts separate static grids, axes, and paths onto one `<Canvas>` layer and cursor crosshairs, dots, and zoom boxes onto an overlay `<Canvas>`, so pointer tracking never redraws series data. Beyond `TimeSeriesChart`, the package includes `LogView` (with live running level histograms), `TraceWaterfall` (`TraceComparison`), `ServiceMap`, `FlameGraph` (`SandwichView`, `diffProfiles`), and bucketed `Heatmap`.

useCasesAndTradeoffs.heading: TypeScript Store vs Opt-In Rust Store (`SeriesBuffer`)
paragraphs: On QuickJS—which runs NSH TSX logic outside the browser—JavaScript heap memory caps at 256 MB and interpreted loops cost roughly 7× more than V8. Upstream README measurements note that the pure TypeScript store holds roughly 2 million samples comfortably, whereas registering `nsh-o11y/native` (`SeriesBuffer` + `lod.rs`) keeps samples in Rust, scales past the 256 MB JS heap limit (tested to 10M+ samples upstream), and traces identical SVG path commands back to JS in integer tenths of a point.

Apps targeting only small or moderate datasets in TSX can skip calling `setNativeBackend` while still benefiting from synchronized cross-panel crosshairs and zoom (`createChartSync`), SLO threshold markers, deploy annotations, dual Y axes, and screen-reader/keyboard navigation.
scenarios: Live infrastructure, APM, or telemetry consoles correlating metrics (`TimeSeriesChart`), logs (`LogView`), traces (`TraceWaterfall`), and CPU profiles (`FlameGraph`) via `createChartSync`.
Streaming dashboards (`append`, sliding `window`, `maxPoints`) that avoid rebuilding decimation trees on every incoming sample batch.
Heavy multi-million-point analysis tools that offload storage from QuickJS's 256 MB heap into Rust `SeriesBuffer`.

installationAndSource.heading: crates.io Installation & Native Store Configuration
installationAndSource.sourceRationale: `nsh-o11y@0.1.0` targets `nsh >= 0.7` (`nsh-core = "0.7.0"` in `Cargo.toml`) and installs straight from crates.io via `nsh add nsh-o11y`.
prerequisites: Requires `nsh >= 0.7` and a local Rust toolchain (`wasm32-unknown-unknown` for Web builds).
Works immediately with TypeScript stores; import `* as native from "nsh-o11y/native"` and call `setNativeBackend(...)` before creating stores to enable Rust-backed `SeriesBuffer`.
When testing from a local `--path` checkout, copy upstream `.cargo/config.toml` optimization settings so Rust `lod.rs` builds do not run unoptimized.

corePurpose.heading: M4 金字塔降采样与双层原生画布架构
paragraphs: `nsh-o11y` 针对百万级采样与实时数据流场景设计：每个序列维护一套以 8、64、512……分块的最小/最大金字塔，渲染每帧像素列时直接采用 M4 降采样（首、最小、最大、末值）。渲染开销只取决于绘图区像素宽度而不随采样总量线性暴涨，且不会丢失单点尖峰毛刺。

在绘制上采用双 `<Canvas>` 分层：底层承载网格、坐标轴与序列路径，顶层专门绘制十字准星、悬停高亮点与框选缩放框，因此移动鼠标不会重绘整条曲线。除核心 `TimeSeriesChart` 外，库内还提供 `LogView`、`TraceWaterfall` / `TraceComparison`、`ServiceMap`、`FlameGraph` / `SandwichView` 及时间分桶 `Heatmap`。

useCasesAndTradeoffs.heading: TS 存储与可选 Rust 存储（`SeriesBuffer`）取舍
paragraphs: 在桌面与移动端使用的 QuickJS Runtime 解释环境中，单个 JS 宿主受限于 256 MB 堆上限且循环执行慢于 V8 引擎。上游实测说明纯 TypeScript 存储可流畅承载约 200 万采样（测试范围涵盖 100k、1M 与 10M 级序列）；若开启 `"nsh-o11y/native"`（`setNativeBackend`），采样点常驻 Rust 侧 `SeriesBuffer` 并由 `lod.rs` 同步执行金字塔与 M4 计算，仅回传整数十分之一点坐标的 SVG 路径给画布，从而绕过 256 MB 内存墙。
多图表联动可通过 `createChartSync()` 共享十字准星与缩放区间，同时内建 SLO 阈值线、发布事件标注、双 Y 轴、色盲安全调色板及键盘与读屏无障碍支持；上游还对比了 uPlot 1.6.32、ECharts 6.1.0、Chart.js 4.6.2、Plotly 4.3.0 与 Dygraphs 2.2.2 在浏览器 Canvas 2D 下的帧耗时表现。
scenarios: 自建 APM、日志监控或系统性能分析工具，在一个界面联动指标（`TimeSeriesChart`）、日志（`LogView`）、链路（`TraceWaterfall`）与火焰图（`FlameGraph`）。

超出 QuickJS 256 MB 堆上限的超大规模时序数据集，开启 `nsh-o11y/native` 交由 Rust 存储处理。

en.title: nsh-webgpu: Native wgpu 29 WebGPU API for NSH
en.metaDescription: Exposes navigator.gpu, GPUDevice, and WebGPU <Canvas> in Native Shell via wgpu 29; marked publish = false in Cargo.toml so install from GitHub.
en.h1: nsh-webgpu: WebGPU Specification Port on wgpu 29 for NSH
en.summary: Hybrid Rust + TSX port of react-native-webgpu onto wgpu 29 by SuperNSH, exposing navigator.gpu, GPUDevice, WGSL pipelines, and <Canvas getContext("webgpu")> across six platforms.

corePurpose.heading: WebGPU Spec Classes Backed by wgpu 29 Instead of Dawn
paragraphs: `nsh-webgpu` ports `react-native-webgpu` to Native Shell by replacing Google Dawn with `wgpu 29`—the same GPU abstraction layer NSH itself uses internally. Inside Rust (`src/lib.rs`), `#[module]` APIs and a handle registry manage `wgpu` instances, buffers, textures, encoders, and per-platform native surface components (`#[native_components(<platform>)]`), while `tsx/index.tsx` exposes spec classes (`GPU`, `GPUDevice`, `GPUBuffer`, `GPUOffscreenCanvas`), `navigator.gpu`, `requestAnimationFrame`, `createImageBitmap`, and hooks (`useDevice`, `useCanvasRef`, `useSurface`, `GPUDeviceProvider`, `useMainDevice`).

Where `wgpu 29` lacks a Dawn-specific upstream extension—such as Dawn device import, platform hardware buffers, or video texture import—the TypeScript exports retain their names and throw structured `ERR_WEBGPU_UNSUPPORTED` errors (`docs/parity.md` lists each case explicitly).

useCasesAndTradeoffs.heading: Comparing nsh-webgpu vs nsh-skia & Platform Caveats
paragraphs: Choose `nsh-webgpu` when writing WGSL compute/render shaders, 3D graphics, or porting existing `react-native-webgpu` codebases across desktop, mobile, and browser WebGPU. Unlike `nsh-skia`, `nsh-webgpu` does run on NSH's Web target (delegating to the browser's native WebGPU) and supports GPU canvas surfaces on mobile emulators.

Be mindful of upstream's candid platform notes: Windows and Linux CI tested software adapters (DX12 on WARP and Vulkan on lavapipe, where `wgpu 29` lacks Import External Texture), Android GLES emulators pass 38 of 44 gallery tests with opaque black clearing (no `alphaMode: "premultiplied"` compositing or `COPY_SRC` surface readback), and physical iPhone, Android, or hardware Windows/Linux GPUs remain explicitly unverified upstream.
scenarios: Custom 3D scenes, compute shaders, and WGSL post-processing shared between NSH desktop/mobile hosts and WebGPU browsers.
Porting `react-native-webgpu` hooks (`useDevice`, `useCanvasRef`) directly into Native Shell TSX applications.
Headless offscreen GPU rendering (`GPUOffscreenCanvas`) and image bitmap decoding in Rust + TSX workflows.

installationAndSource.heading: Why nsh-webgpu Is GitHub-Only (`publish = false`)
installationAndSource.sourceRationale: `Cargo.toml` explicitly sets `publish = false` at the repository root (referencing temporary Git packaging considerations), so `nsh-webgpu` returns 404 on crates.io. Installing via `nsh add github:SuperNSH/webgpu` reads the root `Cargo.toml` and `nsh.json` directly.
prerequisites: Requires `nsh >= 0.7.1` and Rust toolchain `rust-version = "1.97"` (`edition = "2024"`).
Windows `x86_64` MSVC projects can enable the `static-dxc` Cargo feature so `wgpu` uses DXC instead of system FXC for strict WGSL shaders.
Browser target relies on the client browser supporting the WebGPU API.

platformSupport.overview: Upstream `SuperNSH/webgpu` documents exact GPU adapter coverage and explicit exclusions per platform.

matrix.notes: Runs `cargo test`, 89 headless tests, onscreen Triangle/Cube CI, and 44/45 gallery tests.

6 tests fail due to GLES 3.1/GLSL limits; opaque GL surfaces prevent transparent canvas compositing and surface `COPY_SRC`; physical Android untested.

en.title: nsh-skia: Skia 2D Canvas & Shaders for Native Shell
en.metaDescription: Implements react-native-skia primitives and RuntimeEffect on skia-safe with verified macOS Metal and Linux OpenGL GPU views; Web is unsupported.
en.h1: nsh-skia: Skia 2D Drawing & RuntimeEffect Shaders for NSH
en.summary: Hybrid Rust + TSX port of react-native-skia onto skia-safe (rust-skia 0.157.0) by SuperNSH, featuring hardware GPU canvas views verified on macOS Metal and Linux OpenGL.

corePurpose.heading: Declarative Skia Scene Nodes Without a React Reconciler
paragraphs: `nsh-skia` exposes the familiar `react-native-skia` declarative JSX components (`<Canvas>`, `<Circle>`, `<Path>`, `<Fill>`, `<Group>`, `<LinearGradient>`, `<BlurMask>`, `<Mask>`, `<Repeat>`) alongside imperative APIs (`Skia.Path`, `Skia.Paint()`, `Skia.RuntimeEffect`, `Skia.Surface.MakeOffscreen`) and `useClock()` for NSH apps.

Because Native Shell is signal-based rather than React-reconciled, each TSX component instantiates a retained Rust scene node (`scene.rs`). Reactive expressions (`r={r()}`) or accessors update individual node properties directly, and Rust records the Skia frame—exposing native `#[native_module("nsh-skia/native")]` bindings backed by vendored `rust-skia 0.157.0` (`vendor/skia-safe` renames HarfBuzz and `libwebp` symbols on Linux to avoid clashes).

useCasesAndTradeoffs.heading: Pixel Parity, Prebuilt Binary Size & Strict Platform Scope
paragraphs: Upstream compares 48 scenes rendered by `nsh-skia` and upstream `react-native-skia` (on CanvasKit): the 46 non-text scenes drawable in CanvasKit match within at most 2 of 255 in any RGB/alpha channel (`docs/evidence/parity`). Use `<Repeat>` instead of `<Each>` inside `<Canvas>` when scenes exceed 32 rows so every element stays rendered.

Unlike `nsh-webgpu`, `nsh-skia` carries explicit platform boundaries: **Web is completely unsupported** (Skia has no build for NSH's web target), and **iOS, Android, and Windows currently have no GPU canvas view** (they fall back to in-memory snapshots shown as images and were neither built nor run upstream).
scenarios: macOS and Linux desktop apps requiring Skia gradients, `BlurMask`, clipping masks, rich vector paths, or `Skia.RuntimeEffect` shaders.
Server/CLI or desktop offscreen image rendering (`Skia.Surface.MakeOffscreen(256, 256)!.makeImageSnapshot().encode()`).
Porting existing `react-native-skia` 2D artwork to NSH desktop targets using signals/computed in place of Reanimated shared values.

installationAndSource.heading: GitHub-Only Installation & Linux System Library Prerequisites
installationAndSource.sourceRationale: `Cargo.toml` marks `publish = false` at the repository root and vendors two `rust-skia` crates under `/vendor`, so `nsh-skia` is not on crates.io and installs via `nsh add github:SuperNSH/skia`.
prerequisites: Requires Rust `1.97` (`edition = "2024"`), `nsh >= 0.7.1`, and network access during the first Cargo build to download prebuilt `rust-skia` binaries (~18 MB on macOS, ~26 MB on Linux), adding roughly 17–20 MB to packaged app binaries.
Linux builds require glibc `2.35+` and system dev packages: `libgl-dev libegl-dev libgles-dev libwayland-dev libx11-dev libfontconfig1-dev libfreetype-dev`.
Do not target `--target web`; Skia compilation is disabled on `wasm32` (`#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]`).

platformSupport.heading: Platform GPU Verification Matrix
platformSupport.overview: GPU canvas views exist and are verified only on macOS and Linux in `0.1.0`; other targets either fall back in memory or are excluded.

matrix.notes: Dedicated render thread; headless tests and windowed gallery verified on Apple Silicon.
Tested on arm64 X11 and Wayland (weston) with `llvmpipe` software GL; real Linux GPUs and x86-64 windows untested upstream.
No GPU view yet; draws in memory to an image. Upstream notes these targets were not built or run.
Skia has no build for NSH's WebAssembly target.

en.title: nsh-query: Pure-TSX TanStack Query Adapter for NSH
en.metaDescription: Zero Rust toolchain needed: wires @tanstack/query-core hooks and Storage persistence to NSH lifecycle events via github:Dearest/nsh-query.
en.h1: nsh-query: Pure-TSX TanStack Query Adapter for Native Shell
en.summary: Pure-TSX community nshm (nsh.json only, no Cargo.toml) adapting unmodified @tanstack/query-core 5.108.4 with solid-query-style hooks, network reconnects, and NSH Storage persistence.

corePurpose.heading: Why Solid-Style Hooks & NSH Lifecycle Wiring Matter
paragraphs: Because Native Shell components run once and re-evaluate only where reactive signals are read, React Query's re-render semantics do not apply directly. `nsh-query` wraps unmodified `@tanstack/query-core` behind `solid-query`-shaped APIs (`useQuery`, `useMutation`, `useInfiniteQuery`, `QueryClientProvider`), enforcing thunk options (`useQuery(() => ({ ... }))`) and reactive property reads without destructuring (`todo.data` instead of `const { data } = todo`).

`QueryClientProvider` (or `connectNsh()`) maps NSH platform signals directly into `query-core`: `lifecycle() === "background"` pauses polling while returning from background triggers `refetchOnWindowFocus`, `"inactive"` desktop windows keep polling like visible browser tabs unless customized, `wakeCount()` refetches stale queries on system resume, and `network().online` drives pause/resume refetching. The secondary export `nsh-query/persist` (`createNshStoragePersister`, `PersistQueryClientProvider`) persists caches in NSH's 5 MB `Storage` at most once per second.

useCasesAndTradeoffs.heading: Pure-TSX Simplicity & Crucial Name Collision Warning
paragraphs: As the **only pure-TSX module (`tsx-nshm`)** among the 13 verified `nsh 0.7.1` entries, `nsh-query` contains **no `Cargo.toml` and no Rust code**. TSX applications add it without installing Cargo or triggering native crate recompilations, and on desktop multi-window apps one `QueryClient` shares cached responses across every `<Window>` on the engine.

Watch out for two traps documented upstream and in Discovery: **do not** run `nsh add nsh-query` without `github:Dearest/`—a different, non-nshm crate named `nsh-query` (`0.1.0`) exists on crates.io and fails `nsh add`; also **do not** install `@tanstack/query-core` separately next to `nsh-query`, because `nsh-query` vendors its own wired copy.
scenarios: TSX-only NSH applications needing caching, background refetching, optimistic mutations, and offline queue resilience without touching Rust.
Instant cold-start rendering from persisted NSH `Storage` (`PersistQueryClientProvider` with `gcTime >= maxAge`).
Multi-window desktop apps sharing one `QueryClient` cache across windows without duplicate HTTP calls.

installationAndSource.heading: GitHub-Only Installation & Avoiding the crates.io Collision
installationAndSource.sourceRationale: Pure TSX packages without `Cargo.toml` cannot publish to crates.io (`nsh.json` declares `"exports": {"nsh-query": "src/index.ts", "nsh-query/persist": "src/persist/index.ts"}`), and crates.io already holds an unrelated non-nshm `nsh-query` crate. Always specify `github:Dearest/nsh-query`.
prerequisites: No Rust toolchain required when used in a TSX-only NSH application.
Requires `nsh >= 0.6` (verified clean on `nsh 0.7.1`; built around `@tanstack/query-core` `5.108.4`).
When using `PersistQueryClientProvider`, keep `gcTime` at least equal to `maxAge` (default 24 h) so restored queries are not garbage-collected immediately.

platformSupport.heading: Universal TSX Support Across All Six Targets
platformSupport.overview: Because `nsh-query` ships pure TypeScript bundled by `nsh-bundler`, it runs wherever NSH provides QuickJS or Web JS runtimes plus `Storage`, `lifecycle()`, and `network()`.

matrix.notes: Pauses polling on `lifecycle() === "background"` and refetches stale queries on foreground return.
Desktop windows share one engine `QueryClient`; `wakeCount()` triggers stale refetches on computer wake; `"inactive"` remains focused by default.
Bundles via Rolldown alongside `nsh-platform-web` with zero WASM/Rust steps.

companionsOrFeatures.heading: Export Paths & Behavioral Differences from React Query
companionsOrFeatures.summary: Documents key differences upstream explicitly flags in `docs/differences.md`.

items.name: nsh-query
items.detail: Exports `QueryClient`, `QueryClientProvider`, `connectNsh`, `useQuery`, `useMutation`, `useQueries`, `useInfiniteQuery` (`use*` names only, no `create*` aliases).

zh.title: nsh-query：免 Rust 工具链的纯 TSX TanStack Query 适配
zh.metaDescription: 将 useQuery、useMutation 与持久化存储接入 NSH 应用生命周期与网络状态，纯 TSX 模块无需编译 Rust 即可从 GitHub 安装。
zh.h1: nsh-query：纯 TSX 的 TanStack Query 生命周期适配器
zh.summary: 社区维护的纯 TSX 类型 nshm（无 Cargo.toml），将未改动的 @tanstack/query-core 5.108.4 封装为 solid-query 风格 Hooks，并与 NSH 生命周期、网络状态及 Storage 持久化打通。

corePurpose.heading: 适配 NSH 信号模型与平台生命周期
paragraphs: 由于 Native Shell 组件函数只运行一次、仅在读取信号处局部重计算，React Query 的整树重渲染模型并不适用。`nsh-query` 对 `@tanstack/query-core` 采用 `solid-query` 风格封装：配置项必须为函数（`useQuery(() => ({ ... }))`），结果必须按属性访问而不可解构（读取 `todo.data` 而非 `const { data } = todo`）。

`QueryClientProvider`（或 `connectNsh()`）直接桥接 NSH 原生信号：当 `lifecycle()` 进入 `"background"` 时暂停轮询、回到前台重新拉取过期查询；桌面端非焦点可见窗口（`"inactive"`）默认视作可见继续轮询；系统休眠唤醒（`wakeCount()` 增长）和网络重连（`network().online`）自动触发刷新；子路径 `nsh-query/persist` 则可按每秒最多一次写入 5 MB 应用 `Storage`。

useCasesAndTradeoffs.heading: 纯 TSX 优势与必须注意的 crates.io 同名冲突
paragraphs: 在全部 13 个通过 `0.7.1` 实测的模块中，`nsh-query` 是**唯一一个纯 TSX（`tsx-nshm`）模块**，仓库没有 `Cargo.toml`，因此纯 TSX 项目安装它完全不需要配置 Rust 编译器。桌面多窗口应用中，整个引擎共享单一 `QueryClient` 缓存。

安装时务必避开两个关键坑点：第一，**绝对不要**省略 `github:Dearest/` 而运行 `nsh add nsh-query`——crates.io 上存在一个同名但并非 nshm 的 `nsh-query` Rust crate，直接安装必然失败；第二，不要额外手动安装 `@tanstack/query-core`，`nsh-query` 已内置绑定好上下文的版本，重复安装会导致生命周期信号失效。
scenarios: 纯 TSX 开发的跨端应用需要成熟的请求去重、后台自动刷新、乐观更新与离线持久化，同时希望保持零 Rust 构建开销。
利用 `PersistQueryClientProvider` 在应用重启冷启动首帧即刻展示上次缓存数据（注意确保 `gcTime >= maxAge`）。
桌面多窗口场景共用统一缓存，避免跨窗口重复请求。

installationAndSource.heading: 为何仅托管 GitHub 及防同名碰撞指南
installationAndSource.sourceRationale: 纯 TSX 包不包含 `Cargo.toml`，无法上架 Cargo 仓库（由根目录 `nsh.json` 的 `"exports"` 定义 `"nsh-query"` 与 `"nsh-query/persist"`）；且 crates.io 同名 crate 属于其他非 nshm 项目，故必须执行 `nsh add github:Dearest/nsh-query`。
prerequisites: 纯 TSX 项目无需 Rust 工具链即可打包运行。
兼容 `nsh >= 0.6`（已在 `nsh 0.7.1` 验证通过，内部绑定 `query-core 5.108.4`）。
启用持久化时若缓存数据结构变更，请调整 `buster` 参数以失效旧缓存；若 5 MB 空间写满将通过 `removeOldestQuery` 淘汰最旧查询。

en.title: nsmetry: Cookieless Event Analytics SDK for NSH
en.metaDescription: Batch and retry app telemetry from Native Shell clients to a self-hosted Cloudflare Worker and D1 dashboard via the crates.io sdk/nsh package.
en.h1: nsmetry: Privacy-First Event & Screen Analytics SDK for NSH
en.summary: MIT-licensed client telemetry SDK by huacnlee that batches NSH events and <NavStack> screen views with backoff retries toward a self-hosted NsMetry Cloudflare Worker.

corePurpose.heading: Batched App & Screen Telemetry Without Cookies or Crash Risk
paragraphs: NsMetry is an open-source, self-hosted analytics stack running on Cloudflare Workers' free plan with a D1 database—using no cookies, storing no personal data at rest, and hashing optional anonymous install IDs per site on the server. Inside `huacnlee/nsmetry`, the `sdk/nsh/` subdirectory publishes the `nsmetry` client SDK for Native Shell apps alongside an NSH-built client viewer app at the repository root.

The SDK exports `createNsMetry`, `useNsMetry` (flushing automatically when `lifecycle()` moves to `"background"` and best-effort within NSH's 200 ms desktop quit window), `useScreenTracking`, `navStackPath`, and `describePlatform(platform)`. Queued events batch up to `maxBatch: 50` every `flushInterval: 300_000` ms (`maxQueue: 1000` offline cap), retry with backoff, never reject or throw into the host application, and skip redundant `"inactive"` desktop focus changes.

useCasesAndTradeoffs.heading: Monorepo Layout Caveat (`app/` vs `sdk/nsh/`) & Packaging Nuance
paragraphs: Pay close attention to the repository layout when inspecting `huacnlee/nsmetry`: the **repository root** is the full NsMetry viewer/dashboard NSH application (`nsh.json` has `"entry": "app/App.tsx"` and `"id": "dev.nsmetry.app"`), whereas the installable nshm crate lives in `sdk/nsh/`. As a result, **`nsh add nsmetry` works from crates.io**, while `nsh add github:huacnlee/nsmetry` would see the dashboard app root instead of `sdk/nsh`.

Inside `sdk/nsh/Cargo.toml`, the author ships an intentionally empty `native/src/lib.rs` stub (`nsh-core = "0.7.0"`) purely so Cargo can distribute the TypeScript `src/` SDK (`nsh.json` `"exports": {"nsmetry": "src/index.ts"}`) through crates.io.
scenarios: Tracking daily/weekly/monthly active installs, retention, custom events (up to 10 scalar properties), and `<NavStack>` screen transitions without third-party SaaS tracking.
Deploying one Cloudflare Worker + D1 backend (`ADMIN_EMAIL` login, optional OAuth MCP server) serving both NSH mobile/desktop apps and ~2 KB web script sites.
Honoring user opt-outs immediately via `client.setEnabled(false)` (which drops queued events) and `identify(null)`.

installationAndSource.heading: Install from crates.io (Not Root GitHub URL)
installationAndSource.sourceRationale: `sdk/nsh` is published on crates.io as `nsmetry@0.1.0` specifically so `nsh add nsmetry` works seamlessly without hitting the viewer app's root `nsh.json` in `huacnlee/nsmetry`. Always install via `nsh add nsmetry` rather than the GitHub repo root.
prerequisites: Requires `nsh >= 0.7` and a self-hosted NsMetry Cloudflare Worker endpoint configured with `ADMIN_EMAIL` (avoid `*.workers.dev` hostnames in production since ad blockers block them wholesale).
Because `sdk/nsh` wraps an empty Rust target (`native/src/lib.rs`), Rust toolchains build the stub once cleanly with no runtime native hooks.
Keep dynamic entity IDs out of `useScreenTracking` paths (log `/message` rather than `/message/8812`) so dashboard breakdowns remain clean.

platformSupport.heading: Client SDK Behavior Across All Six Platforms
platformSupport.overview: Shares core queue logic (`sdk/js/src/core.ts`) across desktop, mobile, and Web with platform-tailored `User-Agent` formatting.

matrix.notes: `useNsMetry` flushes when `lifecycle()` becomes `"background"`; `describePlatform` reports mobile UA strings.
Avoids flushing on `"inactive"` Cmd-Tab focus changes; performs 200 ms best-effort flush on desktop quit.
`describePlatform` yields `undefined` on Web so the browser's native `User-Agent` header is used.

corePurpose.heading: 无 Cookie 批量埋点与安全退避机制
paragraphs: NsMetry 是一套运行在 Cloudflare 免费套餐（单 Worker + D1）上的开源隐私分析系统，不使用 Cookie、不在存储中保留原始个人身份信息，匿名安装 ID 在服务端按站点加盐哈希。仓库 `huacnlee/nsmetry` 的根目录是完整的 NsMetry 仪表盘应用，而面向应用的客户端 SDK 位于子目录 `sdk/nsh/`。

useCasesAndTradeoffs.heading: Monorepo 目录结构注意事项（`app/` 与 `sdk/nsh/`）

en.h1: nsh-platform-harmonyos: HarmonyOS & OpenHarmony ArkUI Target
en.summary: Community platform nshm maintained by huacnlee (built on ArkUI work originally by @richerfu), enabling `nsh run/package/test --target harmonyos` for HarmonyOS NEXT and OpenHarmony.

corePurpose.heading: External Platform Extension Point Rendering Native ArkUI Views
paragraphs: Rather than shipping inside `longbridge/nsh`, `nsh-platform-harmonyos` is implemented on NSH's public platform extension points (`nsh.json` `"platform": "harmonyos"`). It builds both a host runner CLI (`[[bin]] nsh-platform-harmonyos`) and an N-API ArkUI backend library (`libnsh_platform_harmonyos.so` on `OH_ArkUI_*` and `OH_Drawing_Typography`), rendering Rust, TSX, and mixed Rust+TSX NSH apps inside a stage-model `EntryAbility` + `NshSurface`.

Inside app code, `platform.name === "harmonyos"` while `platform.os === "android"` so Android mobile conventions—such as system back gestures, `android={{...}}` props, and `platform.select({ android })`—apply cleanly. The runner also reads `[package.metadata.nsh.harmonyos]` and feature-scoped `[package.metadata.nsh.features.<name>.harmonyos]` entries (`permissions`, `querySchemes`, `abilities`, `dependencies`, `strings`) from linked crates and merges them into `module.json5` and `oh-package.json5`.

useCasesAndTradeoffs.heading: Community Support Boundary & Device/Emulator Status
paragraphs: Upstream explicitly emphasizes that HarmonyOS is **a community platform outside `longbridge/nsh`**: NSH itself does not ship, test, or support this target, so issues and pull requests belong on `huacnlee/nsh-platform-harmonyos`. On an OpenHarmony 7.0 (API 26) emulator, upstream confirms the TSX gallery and Rust counter build, sign (debug keys), and run via `nsh run --target harmonyos --runtime-os openharmony`, while Huawei phones require DevEco Studio debug or release signing configs (HarmonyOS NEXT 5.0+ shares OpenHarmony's ArkUI C API, NDK, and `aarch64-unknown-linux-ohos` ABI).

en.title: How Native Shell nshm Discovery & Verification Work
en.metaDescription: Empirical results from auditing 119 crates.io crates and 89 GitHub repos on NSH 0.7.1: four manifest kinds, the Cargo 0.6 quirk, and rejection logs.
en.h1: How nshm Modules Are Defined, Discovered & Verified on nsh 0.7.1
en.lead: Empirical methodology behind Awesome NSH: exact manifest rules from longbridge/nsh source code, the Cargo 0.6 table-normalization parser quirk, hit counts across six discovery channels, and full acceptance/exclusion ledgers.
intro: Inspection of `crates/nsh-cli/src/nshm/manifest.rs` (`Manifest::read`), `crates/nsh-cli/src/rust_app.rs` (`specifier_of`), official `nsh.dev/docs/nshm` specs, and live `nsh add` executions in clean scratch apps against `nsh 0.7.1 (f78eace)` shows that crates.io keywords (`keywords = ["nshm"]`) and `nsh-` crate name prefixes do NOT make a package installable.

Because `nsh 0.7.1` includes no built-in package search or directory listing subcommand (`nsh --help` only accepts explicit crate names, `github:owner/repo`, Git URLs, or `--path`), automated catalog curation in `scripts/discover.mjs` must combine six independent upstream channels and verify manifests statically and empirically.

manifestRules.heading: 1. Four Structural Manifest Kinds Accepted by nsh add
manifestRules.intro: An installable `nshm` must satisfy both structural manifest criteria AND NSH semver compatibility (`check_nsh`) against the installed CLI version (`0.7.1`):
rows: #[native_module("<specifier>")] attribute on a line in [lib] path (defaults to src/lib.rs)
Checks nsh-core in [dependencies] (or [workspace.dependencies] via nsh-core.workspace = true) and optional nsh.json "nsh"
"name", semver "version", and non-empty "exports" mapping <name> or <name>/* to existing TSX/TS files
#[native_module("<specifier>")] in Rust crate + "exports" in nsh.json (matching [package] name & version if repeated; export specifiers must not collide with the Rust module specifier)
Checks both Cargo.toml nsh-core and nsh.json "nsh"
nsh.json declares "platform": "<target>" + crate builds binary nsh-platform-<target> (#[native_module] optional)
nuances: An app's `nsh.json` is ignored when `Cargo.toml` is present unless `nsh.json` declares `"exports"` or `"platform"`.

A `Cargo.toml` virtual workspace root fails `nsh add` with `Cargo.toml has no [package] name` (observed directly on `github:SuperNSH/biometrics`). Multi-crate repositories must publish sub-crates to crates.io or place the nshm `[package]` at the repo root (`SuperNSH/webgpu`, `SuperNSH/skia`, `SuperNSH/widgets`, `SuperNSH/icons`).

End-user NSH apps in mixed Rust+TSX mode (`huacnlee/spotish`, `ryujane/Ferrix`, `SuperNSH/starter`) look structurally similar because they also write `#[native_module("...")]` in `src/lib.rs`, yet set `publish = false` and `"root"`/`"id"` instead of `"exports"` in `nsh.json`—so curation must separate them into templates or apps.

cargoPublishQuirk.heading: 2. The Cargo Publish Normalization Parser Quirk in nsh-cli 0.7.1
cargoPublishQuirk.explanation: When `cargo publish` packages a crate tarball, Cargo rewrites inline `[dependencies] nsh-core = "0.6.0"` into a TOML sub-table (`[dependencies.nsh-core] version = "0.6.0"`). Because `manifest.rs::nsh_core_requirement` in `nsh-cli 0.7.1` only scans the `[dependencies]` and `[workspace.dependencies]` tables, it sees `None` for normalized `nsh-core` entries. Consequently, 18 crates.io packages pinned to `nsh-core 0.6` / `0.6.0` (17 `SuperNSH/*` `0.1.0`/`0.0.1` crates plus `nsh-platform-miniprogram@0.1.0`) pass `nsh add` on `nsh 0.7.1` purely due to parser omission, whereas identical GitHub checkouts with un-normalized `[dependencies] nsh-core = "0.6"` are rejected by `check_nsh`. Awesome NSH treats those 18 crates as targeting NSH 0.6 until updated to 0.7 on crates.io.

channelsTable.heading: 3. Six Discovery Channels & Empirical Hit Counts
channelsTable.intro: Running `node scripts/discover.mjs` across all six channels inspected 119 unique crates.io crates and 89 unique GitHub repositories, surfacing 7 clean `0.7.1` crates.io nshms (plus 40 icon-set sub-crates and 3 internal data crates), 6 clean `0.7.1` GitHub/Git nshms, 18 normalized `0.6` crates, and 3 explicitly `0.6`/`=0.7.0` incompatible GitHub nshms.
rows: High signal, but includes 35 supernsh-icons-* + 5 nsh-icon-* companion crates, 17 0.6-pinned SuperNSH/* crates, 3 non-nshm helpers (nsh-frameworks, nsh-native-deps, nsh-maven), and nsh-widgets (0.6 on crates.io).

Catches 18 nsh-core-dependent framework crates, untagged nshms (nsh-platform-harmonyos, nsh-platform-miniprogram lacked nshm keyword in 0.1.0), nsh-ext*, nsh-auth*, nsh-firebase-*, and 3 unrelated crates (bamboo-tui, json-schema-editor, nsh-ui-mobile).
Surfaces nsh-auth, nsh-form, nsh-query (SuperNSH), nsh-http, nsh-firebase-*, maplibre-nsh—mostly plain Cargo libraries or helpers rather than nshms.

Official curated directory powering nsh.dev/directory: 6 installable (nsh-graph, nsh-o11y, nsh-omarchy, nsh-icon, nsh-platform-harmonyos via GitHub, nsh-platform-miniprogram for 0.6) and 4 non-nshm CLI/library repos (shadcn-nsh, hero-nsh, a2ui-nsh, native-shell-with-ns).
topic:nshm returned only 1 unrelated seismic repo; topic:nsh surfaced caoxing9/nsh-shadcn, Dearest/nsh-query, and NSH apps; topic:native-shell returned mostly apps.
Requires exact filename filtering to avoid xonsh.json noise. Critical gap: GitHub Code Search returned 0 results for newly created org:SuperNSH!
Uncovered SuperNSH/webgpu, SuperNSH/skia, and SuperNSH/widgets (master), all missed completely by GitHub Code and Topic Search.

zh.title: Native Shell nshm 发现机制与 nsh add 实测方法论
zh.metaDescription: 基于 119 个 crates.io crate 与 89 个 GitHub 仓库的 NSH 0.7.1 六渠道实测：详述四类合法清单规则、0.6 规范化 quirks 与排除名单。
zh.h1: nshm 模块定义规则、6 渠道发现机制与 0.7.1 实测账本
zh.lead: 系统梳理 Awesome NSH 基于 `longbridge/nsh` 源码与 `nsh 0.7.1 (f78eace)` 真机命令行实测的发现方法：四类合法清单形态、Cargo 0.6 规范化 parser quirk、六渠道命中数与完整拒收账本。
intro: 直接审阅 `longbridge/nsh` 中的 `crates/nsh-cli/src/nshm/manifest.rs`（`Manifest::read`）、`crates/nsh-cli/src/rust_app.rs`（`specifier_of`）、官方 `nsh.dev/docs/nshm` 文档并在独立临时应用中执行 `nsh add` 后可以确认：**crates.io 上的 `keywords = ["nshm"]` 或 `nsh-` 命名前缀并不能让包具备安装资格**。
由于 `nsh 0.7.1` CLI 本身未内置包搜索或列出目录子命令（`nsh add` 仅支持显式 crate 名、`github:owner/repo`、Git URL 或 `--path`），Awesome NSH 的 `scripts/discover.mjs` 通过整合六条外部发现渠道，再结合清单静态分析与真实 `nsh add` 命令给出可复现结果。

manifestRules.heading: 一、`nsh add` 认可的四种合法 nshm 清单结构
manifestRules.intro: 一个包必须同时满足下方“结构入场规则”与“NSH 语义化版本校验（`check_nsh`）”，才能被 `nsh 0.7.1` 正常添加：
rows: [lib] path（默认 src/lib.rs）某行包含 #[native_module("<specifier>")] 属性宏
检查 [dependencies]（或通过 nsh-core.workspace = true 引用 [workspace.dependencies]）中的 nsh-core 及可选 nsh.json "nsh"
声明 "name"、semver "version"，且非空 "exports" 将 <name> 或 <name>/* 映射到真实存在的 TSX/TS 文件
检查可选 "nsh" semver 要求
Rust crate 导出 #[native_module("<specifier>")] 且 nsh.json 声明 "exports"（若重复写 name/version 须与 Cargo 一致，且导出名不可与 Rust specifier 碰撞）
同时校验 Cargo.toml 的 nsh-core 与 nsh.json 的 "nsh"
nsh.json 声明 "platform": "<target>" 且 crate 构建二进制 nsh-platform-<target>（#[native_module] 可选）
同时校验 Cargo.toml 的 nsh-core 与 nsh.json 的 "nsh"
nuances: 存在 `Cargo.toml` 时，除非 `nsh.json` 显式声明了 `"exports"` 或 `"platform"`，否则 `nsh.json` 会被判定为普通应用配置而忽略。

`Cargo.toml` 为虚拟工作区（virtual workspace root）会在 `nsh add` 时直接报错 `Cargo.toml has no [package] name`（实测见于 `github:SuperNSH/biometrics`）。多 crate 仓库必须把子 crate 发布到 crates.io，或将主 nshm `[package]` 放到仓库根目录（如 `SuperNSH/webgpu`、`SuperNSH/skia`、`SuperNSH/widgets`、`SuperNSH/icons`）。

采用混合模式的终端用户应用（如 `huacnlee/spotish`、`ryujane/Ferrix`、`SuperNSH/starter`）在 `src/lib.rs` 中同样写了 `#[native_module("...")]`，结构极易混淆，但它们在 `Cargo.toml` 标注 `publish = false` 并在 `nsh.json` 声明 `"root"`/`"id"` 而非 `"exports"`，需人工/规则筛除。

cargoPublishQuirk.heading: 二、发现 `nsh-cli 0.7.1` 中 Cargo 发布规范化解析绕过现象
cargoPublishQuirk.explanation: 当开发者运行 `cargo publish` 打包上传 crate 时，Cargo 会把平写形式 `[dependencies] nsh-core = "0.6.0"` 规范化改写成 TOML 子表（如 `[dependencies.nsh-core] version = "0.6.0"`）。然而 `nsh-cli 0.7.1` 的 `manifest.rs::nsh_core_requirement` 只扫描 `[dependencies]` 与 `[workspace.dependencies]`，遇到子表形式会误判 `nsh-core` 约束为 `None`。因此 crates.io 上 **18 个仍锁定 `nsh-core 0.6` / `0.6.0` 的 crate**（17 个 `SuperNSH/*` `0.1.0`/`0.0.1` 包及 `nsh-platform-miniprogram@0.1.0`）在 `nsh 0.7.1` 下竟然能绕过检查；而同样的源码从 GitHub 拉取未规范化写法时则会立刻被 `check_nsh` 拒绝。Awesome NSH 坚持按真实约束将其归为 0.6 目标暂缓收录。
